August 20, 2026

Trump administration has lost all 21 election-law cases in federal court

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Democracy Forward president Skye Perryman said the administration is 0 for 21 in cases involving voter data and federal attempts to intervene in elections, with rulings against it including from judges appointed by Republican presidents. Perryman said courts have blocked the use of a modified SAVE database and that discovery is being pursued to establish what the administration is doing before election day. Perryman said the Constitution grants the president no authority over elections, and that lawyers are prepared to challenge any attempt to prevent votes from being cast or counted.

Air Force major detained after calling for Trump's impeachment over Iran war

tags: politics, defence, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Major Jason Watson, described as the first active-duty service member to call for the impeachment and removal of the president and vice president over the war in Iran, has been ordered into pretrial confinement, according to CNN. Watson appeared outside the US Capitol in uniform and later said on CNN that Trump was flagrantly violating the Constitution, breaking the law, engaging in corruption and killing Americans, adding he was willing to pay the highest price for speaking out. The Uniform Code of Military Justice criminalizes contemptuous words directed at the president and other senior officials, and public dissent by active-duty members is rare.

Trump announces sweeping economic campaign against Iran and threatens third countries

tags: politics, defence, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump announced what he called the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country, describing it as economic warfare and isolation against Iran on an unprecedented scale and saying Iran's navy, air force and military factories have been destroyed. He warned that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities provide a lifeline to Iran will face economic consequences, naming oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries and front companies. Separately, the United Arab Emirates suspended trade and financial ties with Iran following a new missile threat.

Trump states North Korea has 57 nuclear weapons as Pyongyang launches missiles

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump said publicly that Kim Jong-un has 57 nuclear weapons and that he will meet the North Korean leader by the end of the year, remarks characterized as disclosing likely classified information; South Korea puts the figure closer to 80 to 120, according to CBS. Trump also suggested South Korea should be penalized for not joining the war in Iran, and pulled back from joint military drills. North Korea responded overnight by launching roughly 10 ballistic missiles, and Kim's sister said she was unaware of any communication between the two leaders and that Pyongyang's posture toward the United States is unchanged.

White House aide Natalie Harp worked a year without a security clearance

tags: politics, surveillance
sources: @aaronparnas

Reporting says Natalie Harp worked at the White House for more than a year while repeatedly declining to complete routine security clearance paperwork, and is only now in the process of obtaining one, despite close proximity to the president and likely access to highly classified information. Maggie Haberman reported that Harp served as a channel through which foreign leaders sought to reach the president. The White House is now searching for the source of the leaks, since the lack of a clearance was known only internally, and the story has displaced the administration's agenda with under 80 days until November's elections.

Disney and ABC sue FCC as Republicans criticize Brendan Carr

tags: media, politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

ABC and Disney have filed a First Amendment lawsuit against the FCC and chairman Brendan Carr alleging retaliation, amid growing Republican criticism from figures including Tom DeLay and Senator John Kennedy. Twenty-one conservative groups sent Carr a letter warning that license renewal should not become a tool for influencing lawful negotiations, and commentators noted Carr's 2019 statement that the FCC must stop micromanaging local broadcasters' business operations. Carr pushed through a party-line vote eliminating the FCC's 39% ownership cap, Trump has nominated a staff attorney to an open commission seat, and the FCC is intervening in negotiations between local stations and the Big Four networks.

US national debt passes $40 trillion as Treasury doubles buyback operations

tags: markets, economy
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

The United States has reached $40 trillion in national debt, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the government will double its operations buying back its own 10- to 30-year securities. The buyback expansion was characterized as a response to weak foreign demand for US debt. Several major hedge funds are reported to be shorting US markets.

Israel opens criminal probes into killings of Hind Rajab and Gaza aid workers

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Israel has opened criminal investigations into the killings of Hind Rajab and 15 emergency and aid workers in Gaza. The investigations are being conducted by the military.

Israel building execution facility overseen by Ben-Gvir

tags: legal, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Israel is constructing gallows intended for people it designates as terrorists, in a project overseen by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. The plans include a front-row viewing area for the families of those executed. The project was discussed in the Knesset in March of this year and required sign-off from multiple officials.

National Guard mentioned in 1.3% of Washington criminal cases

tags: policing, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

A Reuters review of criminal cases in Washington, D.C. found National Guard troops were mentioned in just 1.3% of them. The finding bears on the deployment's stated purpose of preventing crime in the capital.

Trump's second reduction of Bears Ears followed within a day by mining claims

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

On July 13, 2026, a proclamation cut Bears Ears National Monument from 1.36 million acres to 121,000 acres and terminated the Bears Ears Commission, the tribal body that co-managed the land, naming uranium, vanadium, copper, silver, lead, molybdenum and zinc as the reason. The five tribes that co-managed the monument were not consulted despite a written Interior commitment to do so, and no hearing was held, in contrast to the 2016 public testimony process that preceded the original designation. One day after the proclamation, a mining company filed seven claims on land removed from the monument, though claims cannot legally be staked until September 11. Advocates cite more than 100,000 cultural and archaeological sites in the area and $12 billion in annual outdoor recreation spending in Utah.

GAO finds Pentagon still unable to track troops' blast exposure

tags: defence, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Government Accountability Office reported that the Department of Defense continues to face gaps in tracking service members' exposure to blasts and monitoring their brain health.

DOJ process could restore federal gun rights for some veterans

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Justice Department is establishing a process through which some veterans who lost their federal firearm rights may apply to have them restored.

Byron Donalds wins Florida Republican nomination for governor

tags: politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Byron Donalds, endorsed by Trump, has been nominated by Florida Republicans as their candidate for governor. Donalds has spoken against DEI and equity initiatives, disputed the 2020 election result, and backs stricter border enforcement and deportations.

St. George issues first orange energy alert of the season amid heat

tags: climate, energy
sources: @ericmoutsos

The city of St. George, Utah issued its first orange alert of the season on Tuesday as demand for electricity ran high across the region because of heat, and the call for energy conservation extended into Wednesday. The city has also offered residents an app to track water usage and identify potential leaks.

Texas halts pet adoptions over screwworm outbreak, thousands of animals at risk

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Texas has put adoptions on hold for thousands of dogs and cats as state and federal officials work to stop the spread of the New World screwworm, according to the Associated Press, leaving animals at risk of euthanasia. It is the first time in 60 years the insect has crossed into the United States, and it threatens the cattle industry while also able to infect pets. Many states have restricted animal movement, leaving Texas shelters overcrowded and unable to transfer animals elsewhere for adoption. The outbreak was attributed in part to federal cuts made under DOGE.

Army unit offers four-day GTA VI pass as reenlistment incentive

tags: defence, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The Army's 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia, part of the 3rd Infantry Division, is offering soldiers a special four-day pass timed to the November 19 release of Grand Theft Auto VI in exchange for reenlisting for two to six more years. Soldiers signing contracts between August 1 and November 14, 2026 are eligible, and about 130 soldiers qualify. At least 20 have taken the incentive, according to CBS.

Military recruiting is surging

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Military recruiting across the services is rising, prompting questions about what is driving young Americans to enlist.

VA tests semaglutide as treatment for alcohol use disorder in veterans

tags: health
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Department of Veterans Affairs is running a trial to test whether semaglutide can help veterans with alcohol use disorder reduce their drinking.

FDA raises frozen blueberry recall to highest risk level over E. coli

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas

The FDA upgraded a recall of frozen blueberries and mixed berries sold at Publix stores in several states to its highest health risk classification, reserved for products where exposure could cause serious adverse health consequences or death. The affected items are GreenWise organic whole blueberries in 10-ounce and 48-ounce sizes and GreenWise organic whole mixed berries in 10-ounce and 48-ounce sizes. The cause is potential E. coli contamination.

Gary, Indiana without power for over a week after storm

tags: climate
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Gary, Indiana has been without electricity for more than a week following a severe storm, with residents unable to travel from their streets or get to work. The outage has drawn little national coverage. The city's economic conditions were cited as a reason for the limited response.

Trump arrives late to cryptocurrency and technology speech

tags: politics, media
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Trump was late to a scheduled address on cryptocurrency and technology in Washington, leaving industry figures waiting on stage during live coverage.
